title: Beating procrastination
examples: What is the best way to start a really big project?
Can making a plan actually help me stop putting things off?
How do I remember to use these techniques when I feel lazy?

explain.say: Today we are talking about beating procrastination. Procrastination means putting off things you should do. It is like delaying important work until later.
Our first tool is tiny starts. This means breaking a big task into very small pieces. You only need to focus on the first tiny step.

items: → Tiny Step (e.g., Write one topic sentence)

explain.say: For example, if you must read a long chapter, do not think about the whole thing. Just promise yourself you will read for five minutes only.

draw.text: Example: Read for just five minutes.

explain.say: Next we learn about implementation intentions. This is planning exactly when and where you will work. It makes your plan very specific.

draw.text: Intentions: When and where to act.

explain.say: For instance, instead of saying 'I will study later', you say 'When I finish maths, I will sit at my desk and make flashcards for twenty minutes'.
In real life, you use this when you need to clean your room. Instead of 'I will clean soon', you say 'When I eat dinner, I will put all the books on the shelf'.

faq.q: Why is it so hard to just start doing my homework?
faq.a: It is hard because big tasks feel overwhelming. Tiny starts help by making the first step feel very small and easy to manage.
asks: Why do I feel so resistant to starting?
What helps me overcome the initial resistance?

faq.q: Does making a plan really work for stopping me from delaying things?
faq.a: Yes, implementation intentions work because they remove guesswork. You are telling your brain exactly what to do when a trigger happens.
asks: Is planning enough to stop procrastination?
How does setting a plan help my behaviour?

faq.q: If I break a task down, do I have to finish every tiny step?
faq.a: No, the goal is just to start. If you complete one tiny step, that is a big success and builds momentum for the next one.
asks: What if I only do one tiny step?
Is it okay if I stop after one small part?

faq.q: Can I use this for things that are not schoolwork?
faq.a: Absolutely. You can use these skills for anything, like cleaning your room or getting ready for a trip. The principle is always the same.
asks: Does this only work for studying?
Can I use this for chores?

faq.q: If I forget my plan, what should I do?
faq.a: If you forget, just pause and ask yourself what the trigger was. Then, quickly repeat your specific plan to yourself.
asks: How do I remember my intentions?

facts: Procrastination is the act of delaying or postponing tasks.
Tiny starts focus only on the very first, smallest action needed.
Implementation intentions link a specific trigger to a specific action.
Specificity in planning is key to making habits stick.

quiz.say: To start writing a big report, what is the best first step according to tiny starts?

options.show: Make a detailed outline for all sections.
options.say: Make a detailed outline for all sections.

quiz.why: This is the smallest, easiest piece, which helps you overcome the initial hurdle of starting.

wrong.0: This is still too big and might feel overwhelming right away.
wrong.1: This is research, not the actual starting action for writing.
wrong.2: Outlining is good, but the first action must be even smaller than that.

quiz.say: You want to start revising history notes. You decide: 'When I finish my lunch, I will sit at the dining table and review the causes of World War One for fifteen minutes.' What technique did you use?
quiz.why: You linked a specific time (after lunch), place (dining table), and action (reviewing notes).

wrong.1: Goal setting is what you want to achieve, not the exact plan to get there.
wrong.2: Time blocking is scheduling time, but this includes the 'when' and 'where' trigger too.
wrong.3: Chunking is breaking the task, but this question asks about the timing of the task.

quiz.say: Which statement best shows a 'tiny start' for cleaning your messy desk?

options.show: Put all the books back on the shelf.
options.say: Put all the books back on the shelf.

options.show: Throw away all the old papers.
options.say: Throw away all the old papers.

quiz.why: This is the absolute smallest physical action you can take right now to begin the process.

wrong.1: This is a medium-sized task, not the smallest possible action.
wrong.2: This requires decision-making about what to throw away, which is too big.
wrong.3: Organizing is a multi-step process, not a single tiny action.
